claim_resolution.rationale: Digital Realty's current facility page identifies IAD14 at 43791 Devin Shafron Drive, Building D, matching the mapped facility and advertising current data-center services. The stated 135,000 square feet is explicitly the total building size.

A 2024 Loudoun County permit identifies the exact 43831 Devin Shafron Drive data-center building and Amazon Data Services as applicant for a $2.5 million alteration. Exact-address data-center work supports current operation; no third-party capacity estimate is accepted.

Prince William County's current GIS labels IAD59 planned with no occupancy date, while the county's 2024 inventory identifies the same address and parcel as operational. The official-source conflict prevents classification.

Prince William County's current GIS labels IAD52 planned with no occupancy date, while the county's 2024 inventory identifies the same address and parcel as operational. The official-source conflict prevents classification.

Microsoft reports active operations across two Quincy campuses with more than twenty buildings, and Washington Ecology maintains current Microsoft Quincy permit records. Neither source maps this unnamed IM3 building footprint to a facility code, so building status remains unresolved.

Microsoft reports active operations across two Quincy campuses with more than twenty buildings, and Washington Ecology maintains current Microsoft Quincy permit records. Neither source maps this second unnamed IM3 building footprint to a facility code, so building status remains unresolved.

New Albany identifies an active Google data-center site, and Google recruits operations staff in New Albany. Neither source maps the active buildings to the IM3 label NBY-1, so campus evidence is retained without a building classification.

New Albany publishes multiple AWS building projects and mixed campus lifecycle evidence, but it does not map CMH53 to a named building. Project evidence is retained without assigning a building status.

Equinix's current facility page identifies SV1 at 11 Great Oaks Boulevard and offers active colocation and interconnection products with 24/7 security. The reported 82,850 square feet is colocation space, not total building area, and is therefore not published as building floor area.

Lumen's 2025 data sheet confirms a current Sunnyvale colocation market, and a legacy CenturyLink guide lists SN1 and SN2. The current source does not identify which Sunnyvale building remains represented by the IM3 label Sunnyvale 1, so status remains unresolved.
Lumen lists Phoenix as a current colocation market, but the record supplies no site address or facility code linking that market to the mapped building at 215 East Indian School Road.
Flexential's current Deer Valley facility page offers tours and active colocation services and reports facility-specific critical-load capacity.
Umatilla's wastewater plan establishes an existing PDX2 campus with measured flows, but the public record does not map the combined operator code PDX51/54 to this building footprint.
Umatilla's wastewater plan establishes an existing PDX2 campus with measured flows, but the public record does not map the combined operator code PDX57/60 to this building footprint.
Lumen lists San Antonio as a current colocation market, but the record supplies no site address or facility code linking that market to the mapped building at 215 Rivas Street.

Microsoft confirms operating datacenters in Bexar County and identifies the mapped Wiseman Boulevard project, but its construction update explicitly says construction completion does not indicate operation or availability. The specific building remains unresolved.
